_comment: Per-carrier CSS selector for the article body within a captured page. Stage 2 extracts ONLY from this container. Page chrome is most of the text on these sites — on Ryanair's help centre the article is 1,906 characters and the surrounding navigation is another 578, including a 40-language country picker. Extracting from whole-page text would pull dimensions and weights out of navigation, and a wrong figure is worse than a missing one. A selector that matches nothing is a hard failure, never a fallback to the whole page. Selectors are derived empirically from captured HTML — scored across all of a carrier's pages for presence and text coverage — never guessed from class names.

ryanair.note: Zendesk help centre. Stable across all six captured pages.

qantas.note: Derived empirically from the six manual captures of 2026-08-24. #main-content and main select the identical node on all six pages; the id is used because it is stable across the en-au and en-gb templates. Captures 89% of body innerText.

air-canada.note: Scored 65% of page text across 4 pages; [role=main] is the same element. .content is a 5% fragment.

finnair.note: 88% across 3 pages. .main-content is equivalent; main is the stabler choice.

jetblue.note: 88% across 4 pages. The only candidate present on every page.

westjet.note: 85%. .cmp-container scored 100%, which is the whole page including nav — coverage that high means the selector is not isolating anything.

american-airlines.note: Derived from all six successful 2026-08-24 captures. The same main#main-content container is present on every page and covers 84–99% of body text while excluding the site header and footer.

frontier.note: Derived from all six successful 2026-08-24 captures. Frontier splits article content across sibling article blocks, so the stable section.main-torso parent is required; it excludes navigation, footer, and the large email-signup form.

tap-portugal.note: Derived from both successful 2026-08-24 captures. The stable main#main-content container covers 79–87% of body text and excludes site navigation and footer content.

malaysia-airlines.note: Derived from the successful 2026-08-24 baggage capture. The main element isolates the 942-character baggage landing-page body from navigation, alerts, and footer content; the capture links to detail pages rather than embedding their rules.

rex.note: Derived from the successful 2026-08-24 baggage capture. The legacy page has no semantic main element; #BaggageTab isolates the cabin, checked, excess, and prohibited-baggage panels while excluding the large site menus.
